{{Current events|year=2025|month=01|day=8|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[2025 N'Djamena attack]]
***Gunfire and military vehicles are reported near the [[Official residence#Chad|Presidential Palace]] in [[N'Djamena]], [[Chad]], with the [[Government of Chad|Chadian government]] accusing [[Boko Haram]] of being behind the attack. The [[Chad National Army]] has reportedly regained stable control of the capital, with 18 insurgents and one security force member being killed in the attack. [https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3219554-tense-moments-in-ndjamena-gunfire-near-presidential-palace (Devdiscourse)] [https://www.dw.com/en/chad-gunfire-heard-near-presidency-in-ndjamena/a-71251244 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Israeli Air Force|Israeli airstrikes]] across the [[Gaza Strip]] kill at least 27 people. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2585653/middle-east (Arab News)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Zaporizhzhia strikes (2022–present)|Zaporizhzhia strikes]], [[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] attack an industrial facility in [[Zaporizhzhia]], [[Ukraine]], killing 13 people and injuring 18 others. Further strikes on Zaporizhzhia with [[Aerial bomb|guided aerial bombs]] kill 13 more people and injure 32 others. [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/01/8/7492571/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'')] [https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/01/8/7492614/ (''Ukrainska Pravda'' 2)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2025 Point Triple attack]]
***Twenty-eight [[Benin Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed during a [[mass shooting]] in northern [[Benin]] near the border with [[Burkina Faso]]. [https://punchng.com/28-beninese-soldiers-killed-in-attack-near-burkina-faso-border/ (Punch)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**At least 40 people are killed and 12 others are injured in [[Tatmadaw]] airstrikes on [[Ramree]], [[Rakhine State]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/1/11/dozens-killed-in-myanmar-military-air-attack-in-rakhine-state-un (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/myanmar-army-airstike-12-killed-500-house-destroyed-rakhine-state-2663336-2025-01-11 (''India Today'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 California wildfires]]
**[[January 2025 Southern California wildfires]]
***[[Palisades Fire]], [[Eaton Fire]], [[Hurst Fire]]
****More than 100,000 people are evacuated from approaching [[wildfires]] in the [[Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles|Pacific Palisades]] and [[Hollywood, Los Angeles|Hollywood]] neighborhoods of [[Los Angeles]] and [[Altadena, California|Altadena]], [[California]], [[United States]], that have burnt more than 3,000 acres, aggravated by an ongoing extreme [[windstorm]] and [[Drought|drought conditions]]. Five people are killed, dozens of others are injured, and around 1,000 structures are destroyed. [https://apnews.com/live/live-updates-wildfire-los-angeles-palisades (AP)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/pacific-palisades-fire-la-california-map-latest-b2675408.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/wildfires/live-blog/live-updates-pacific-palisades-wildfire-rapidly-grows-california-rcna186685 (NBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/palisades-fire-live-tens-thousands-flee-wildfires-rage-los-angeles-2025-01-08/ (Reuters)]
***The [[Calnev Pipeline|CALNEV Pipeline]] connecting [[oil refinery|oil refineries]] in [[southern California]] to [[Clark County, Nevada]], shuts down due to [[power outage]]s, temporarily cutting off the [[gasoline]] supply to [[Las Vegas]] and [[Nellis Air Force Base]]. The [[Kinder Morgan]] SFPP Pipeline connecting southern California to [[Phoenix, Arizona]], also shuts down. [https://www.ktnv.com/news/good-morning-las-vegas/good-morning-las-vegas-fuel-supply-concerns-swirling-as-wildfires-disrupt-california-pipelines (KTNV)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/kinder-morgan-fuel-pipelines-shut-due-power-outages-southern-california-2025-01-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[List of deadly human stampedes in Hindu temples|Deadly human stampedes in Hindu temples]]
**Six people are killed and over forty others are injured in a [[stampede]] at the [[Hinduism|Hindu]] [[Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala|Venkateswara Temple]] in [[Tirupati]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://apnews.com/article/india-stampede-andhra-pradesh-temple-7855dcf993849b31f78de56f988058e8 (AP)] [https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/tirupati-stampede-6-dead-40-injured-as-devotees-rush-to-get-tickets-for-vaikunta-dwara-darshanam-460093-2025-01-09 (Business Today)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Italy relations]]
**The [[Government of Iran|Iranian government]] releases [[Italy|Italian]] journalist [[Cecilia Sala]] from prison, with Sala arriving back in [[Rome]] later that day. [https://www.euronews.com/2025/01/08/tehran-releases-italian-journalist-cecilia-sala-from-prison (Euronews)] [https://uk.news.yahoo.com/italian-journalist-cecilia-sala-arrives-040525478.html?guccounter=1 (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Lithuania–Russia relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Lithuania|Lithuanian prime minister]] [[Gintautas Paluckas]] deploys [[Lithuanian Police Force|the police]] to secure [[Lithuania|the country]]'s [[LitPol Link|electricity link]] with [[Poland]] in response to reported attempts to disrupt the planned decoupling of the [[Baltic states]]' power systems from [[IPS/UPS|the grid shared]] with [[Belarus]] and Russia. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/lithuania-boosts-power-grid-security-ahead-russia-decoupling-2025-01-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Azerbaijan]] [[Diplomatic correspondence|protests]] [[Eritrea]]'s detention of three Azerbaijani-flagged vessels and 18 crew members since November 2024, stating the ships entered Eritrean waters due to adverse weather en route to [[Abu Dhabi]], [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/azerbaijan-protests-eritrea-over-detention-three-vessels-crews-2025-01-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] freezes the assets of [[Neo-Nazism|neo-Nazi]] music network [[Blood & Honour]], becoming the first [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right group in the UK]] to be sanctioned by the government. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqjzj4zrppko (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of New Caledonia]]
**{{ill|Alcide Ponga|fr}} of the pro-France [[The Rally (New Caledonia)|The Rally]] party is elected [[President of New Caledonia]] by six of the eleven government ministers. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/538534/alcide-ponga-is-new-caledonia-s-new-president (Radio New Zealand)]
*The ruling party in [[São Tomé and Príncipe]], [[Independent Democratic Action]], proposes [[Hélio Vaz de Almeida]] as [[Prime Minister of São Tomé and Príncipe|Prime Minister]] to replace [[Patrice Trovoada]], who was fired by [[President of São Tomé and Príncipe|President]] [[Carlos Vila Nova]] two days ago. [https://www.rfi.fr/pt/%C3%A1frica-lus%C3%B3fona/20250108-s%C3%A3o-tom%C3%A9-e-pr%C3%ADncipe-adi-prop%C3%B5e-h%C3%A9lio-almeida-para-novo-primeiro-ministro (RFI)]
